gpt-4.basis: MoE architecture (~1.8T total, ~220B active per token). Energy scaled for active parameters only.

gpt-4-turbo.basis: Estimated ~25% efficiency gain over GPT-4 base, MoE active params.

gpt-4o.basis: Jegham et al. (2025) 'How Hungry is AI?' - Hardware measurements in commercial datacenters. Non-linear model: short (<1k tokens), medium (1k-5k), long (>5k). Source: arXiv:2505.09598

gpt-3.5-turbo.basis: Dense architecture (~20B), optimized batching. Active = total for dense models.

claude-3-opus.basis: Dense ~175B parameter model. Full parameter activation per token.

claude-3-haiku.basis: Dense ~20B parameter model, optimized for speed.

claude-3.5-sonnet.basis: Dense ~70B, improved efficiency over Claude 3 Sonnet.

gemini-1.5-pro.basis: MoE architecture (~500B total, ~100B active per token).

llama-3-70b.basis: Dense 70B. Meta published training energy reverse-scaled for inference.

mixtral-8x7b.basis: MoE with 8 experts, 2 active. 47B total, ~13B active per token.

mixtral-8x22b.basis: MoE with 8 experts, 2 active. 141B total, ~39B active per token.

gpt-4.1-nano.basis: Jegham et al. (2025) measured: 0.271 Wh for medium prompt (1k in, 1k out). Most energy-efficient model in benchmark. Source: arXiv:2505.09598

gpt-4.1-mini.basis: Jegham et al. (2025) measured: 0.847 Wh for medium prompt (1k in, 1k out). Source: arXiv:2505.09598

o1.basis: Jegham et al. (2025) measured: 12.1 Wh for medium prompt (1k in, 1k out). Reasoning model with extended chain-of-thought. 40x more energy than GPT-4.1 nano. Source: arXiv:2505.09598

o3.basis: Jegham et al. (2025) measured: 21.414 Wh for medium prompt (1k in, 1k out). Advanced reasoning model. 79x more energy than GPT-4.1 nano. Source: arXiv:2505.09598

deepseek-r1.basis: Jegham et al. (2025) measured: 29.0 Wh for medium prompt (1k in, 1k out). Most energy-intensive model in benchmark. 107x more energy than GPT-4.1 nano. Source: arXiv:2505.09598

claude-3.7-sonnet.basis: Jegham et al. (2025) measured: 2.781 Wh for medium prompt (1k in, 1k out). Ranked highest in eco-efficiency among large models. Source: arXiv:2505.09598
